---|---|---|---
| | |
### SENATE UPDATE: Fighting Back Against Trump's Lawlessness While Delivering for Marylanders
As we continue to face huge challenges in our nation's capital, I want to be clear about two things: I am fighting back every day against a lawless Trump Administration, AND I'm fighting to deliver results that make a real difference in people's lives.

I know many Marylanders are both frustrated and angry by what they see coming out of Washington. I am too. Marylanders are also concerned about the struggles they are facing every day to make ends meet amidst rising costs. I am too.

Those twin challenges are at the heart of the work I do every day in the Senate - from standing up to the Trump Administration's abuses of power to fighting to advance measures that strengthen economic opportunity and lower costs for working families.

Here's the latest on all these fronts:
---
### Standing Up to Trump's Lawless Mass Deportation Agenda
Republicans in Washington are once again making their priorities clear: instead of working to lower costs and make life more affordable for Americans, they are hellbent on providing a blank check for Trump's lawless ICE operations. Americans are struggling with skyrocketing prices on everything from gas to food costs because of Trump's illegal war in Iran, and people are facing steeper health care premiums after Republicans let ACA tax credits expire.

Yet, instead of working with us to end this war and reduce costs, Senate Republicans used what's known as a ["budget reconciliation"](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.youtube.com%2fshorts%2fQOVEQch9Tks&redir_log=304150846172290) bill to bypass normal Senate spending bill procedures in order to stuff an already bloated and out-of-control ICE operation with tens of billions more of taxpayers' dollars. This is on top of the record $75 billion - seven times higher than the normal annual amount - that Republicans gave to ICE last year, and despite the fact that tens of billions of dollars remain unspent as of the end of April.

Last Thursday, we debated and voted all night in the Senate, where Republicans refused to support our efforts to rein in ICE misconduct and opposed over 20 amendments to stop this Administration's rampant abuses. Their stonewalling included blocking [an amendment](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.youtube.com%2fshorts%2f_BgH6zMqPb8&redir_log=111957402837288) I offered with Senator Cassidy to make clear that Trump could not use his DOJ's proposed taxpayer-funded slush fund to provide payouts to January 6th insurrectionists and violent criminals. Instead, we required that those funds could be used ONLY to [compensate law enforcement officers](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.youtube.com%2fshorts%2fWkRu6pAxnzE&redir_log=200779129334295) who were injured defending our Capitol on January 6th and members of their families who suffered harm as a result. Senate Republicans also blocked [my amendment](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mnjpp6ssi22z&redir_log=18662014831446) to prevent violent criminals and those who have committed crimes against children from receiving payouts from the Trump taxpayer slush fund.

I made my position clear on this reckless bill once again: [I voted NO](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mnjsm4lpvc27&redir_log=874701460275444) because - as I've said repeatedly - I will not support one more dime for a lawless ICE operation that refuses to make [meaningful reforms](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mndwl73ixk2j&redir_log=998314602841444). Nevertheless, Senate Republicans voted to give ICE a blank check and, yesterday, House Republicans did the same thing.

I've also been hearing directly from many of you about the real-life impacts of the Administration's cruel mass deportation agenda, including the ongoing pause on application processing at U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) that is disrupting people's ability to work, support their families, and plan for their futures. These impacts extend far beyond work authorizations and are affecting a wide range of applications, often with no clear exemptions or timelines.

Please know that I hear you. I am actively engaged on these issues. I'm pressing the Administration for answers and relief - including urging [DHS Secretary Mullin and USCIS Director Edlow](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fnews%2fpress-releases%2fvan-hollen-alsobrooks-warner-kaine-raise-concerns-over-blanket-pause-on-immigration-decisions-based-on-national-origin&redir_log=85331057351204) to take immediate steps to resume the orderly processing of immigration and naturalization applications. While the recent [court ruling](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mnkwt3dmyk2u&redir_log=031665551862450) that the government must restart asylum and immigration processing is a step in the right direction, we must keep fighting back. Your stories matter, and they are informing the work I'm doing every day in the Senate.
### Demanding Accountability from Todd Blanche, Kash Patel & Trump's Cronies
As the Trump Administration pushes for massive spending at agencies like ICE, Congress has a responsibility to examine how taxpayer dollars are being used across the federal government - including at the Department of Justice and the FBI.

That's why, as the lead Democrat of the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on Commerce, Justice, Science, and Related Agencies - which has jurisdiction over the Department of Justice and FBI funding - I recently used two hearings on the President's FY27 Budget Requests to press Trump Administration officials on corruption, abuses of power, and the politicization of law enforcement.

During [a hearing](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fyoutu.be%2fQSi5UieU4sA%3fsi%3d2ddfoW3hqzTB9tkA&redir_log=929340071379321) last month with Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche - who Trump has now nominated to be the Attorney General - I laid out examples of the horrible actions taken by the Trump DOJ. Blanche himself has been at the center of some of this Administration's most troubling scandals, from helping bury the Epstein files to overseeing a newly proposed $1.8 billion taxpayer-funded slush fund to provide payouts to Trump allies. During the hearing, I asked the Acting Attorney General if those who assaulted police officers on January 6th, and a pardoned January 6th rioter who was since convicted of molesting two children, would be eligible for payouts. [He couldn't say no](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mmajuvpzak2f&redir_log=888813757752451). I am working to eliminate this fund outright. In the meantime, as discussed above, I [offered an amendment](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mmckmrkbts26&redir_log=805203184796447) on the Republican reconciliation bill to prevent anyone convicted of violent crimes or crimes against children from [getting a penny](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mnjpp6ssi22z&redir_log=18662014831446) of your tax dollars.

After the hearing, we also learned that, as part of this scheme to create the slush fund, Blanche also quietly [signed a deal](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mma4sdv77c2q&redir_log=456013694166440) to bar the IRS from ever reexamining Trump's, his family's, or his companies' prior taxes. This is unacceptable.

While Blanche has more recently said he does not intend to proceed with the slush fund, all we have is his word to go on as Trump continues to say [he "loves" it](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mng6gygwmk2s&redir_log=337846168538449). Obviously, Blanche's word isn't good enough. What's more, he's confirmed the Trump family tax scheme still remains intact. I will not stop fighting back against both.

I also pressed FBI Director Kash Patel about [credible reporting](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.youtube.com%2fshorts%2fQy4JBnJg6W8&redir_log=085374488817284) that his conduct and excessive drinking have interfered with his ability to perform his duties. I made clear: I don't give a damn what people do in their private lives, but when that conduct compromises their ability to protect and serve the American people, it's unacceptable. Patel responded by lashing out and making false statements and provable lies - while [refusing to acknowledge](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mlosifz5tc2w&redir_log=458006936556449) that it is a crime to lie to Congress. I also sought answers on his misuse of FBI resources - including diverting agents away from counterintelligence and violent crime investigations in order to pursue political vendettas and support Trump's mass deportation agenda.

Both hearings reinforced the corrupt reality of this Administration: under Donald Trump, agencies that are supposed to protect the public and uphold the rule of law are increasingly being weaponized to do Trump's personal bidding. Every taxpayer dollar spent on political retaliation, corruption, or abuse is a dollar not being spent on keeping Americans safe or improving people's lives. I will continue using every tool available to demand transparency, expose abuses of power, and ensure that no Administration is above the law.
### Pushing Back Against Blank Checks for Endless Wars
At the same time, I am fighting back against Trump's disastrous leadership on the global stage, as we are now over 100 days into the illegal war he and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu launched against Iran. Fourteen Americans have been killed and hundreds wounded. Thousands of civilians throughout the region have been killed. The Strait of Hormuz remains blocked, and [gas prices](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mkq2izlask22&redir_log=321392687058444) remain high while [grocery costs](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mlo76dznlc2w&redir_log=602401249556445) keep going up. Trump revealed his views when [he admitted](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mly7do6jak2q&redir_log=477783471083444): "I don't think about Americans' financial situation." Meanwhile, the Trump Administration admitted that it has spent $29 billion of your tax dollars on this war in just the first two months. At that rate, which was reportedly a lowball estimate, the costs would be over $40 billion as of today.

When you are digging yourself into a hole, [just stop digging](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.youtube.com%2fwatch%3fv%3dPontP7kQMoM&redir_log=184286257845297)!

I have also pressed Secretary Hegseth for answers and [demanded transparency](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fnews%2fpress-releases%2fvan-hollen-warren-open-new-investigation-into-hegseths-role-in-dismantling-militarys-civilian-harm-prevention-guard-rails&redir_log=418557146851232) after he dismantled key Department of Defense offices tasked with preventing civilian casualties, like the Tomahawk missile strike that killed over 120 Iranian school children. These safeguards exist for a reason: to protect innocent lives. Their removal raises urgent questions about compliance with U.S. and international law. But Secretary Hegseth dismissed those concerns and even said that the rules of engagement were "stupid" - rules designed to prevent innocent people from getting killed in war.

I've gone to the [Senate floor](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.youtube.com%2flive%2f5UgAWFJwP-4&redir_log=936784909569264) many times to [call on Republicans](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fnews%2fpress-releases%2frepublicans-block-senate-democrats-war-powers-resolution-once-again-voting-to-continue-trumps-unjustified-unpopular-and-costly-iran-war&redir_log=429172601651332) to support the eight War Powers Resolutions we've brought up to end this illegal war of choice and reclaim Congress's constitutional authority. And I've introduced my own War Powers Resolution as part of that effort, because the Constitution is clear: the power to declare war resides with Congress precisely because our Founding Fathers feared putting that power in the hands of one impulsive president.

Meanwhile, Trump and his Administration are openly musing about yet another illegal, unauthorized military intervention, this time in Cuba, as I spoke about on the [Senate floor](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.youtube.com%2flive%2fKBD4rZ6eyf8&redir_log=974998839309269).

It's failures like these that are hurting Americans at home and hurting our stature abroad. When Secretary Rubio appeared recently before the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, I laid out some of these failures [to him directly](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.youtube.com%2fwatch%3fv%3daENJ9k5pI20&redir_log=790273707616284).

Instead of taking responsibility for these disastrous policies, ending the war in Iran, or reversing course in Cuba, Rubio, Hegseth, and the Trump Administration are asking Congress to approve a [massive increase](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mk3u4cht6c2g&redir_log=872140512847439) in Pentagon spending. After pushing through a $1 trillion defense budget last year, they are proposing nearly $500 billion more - bringing total military spending to roughly $1.5 trillion.

I will not provide one more dime for the illegal war against Iran, and I will not support a bloated Pentagon budget - because that is not what is best for the people of the United States. I will continue to stand up for the Constitution, demand accountability, and focus on the priorities that matter to the American people.
### Defending Our Democracy and the Right to Vote
The strength of our democracy depends on both the rule of law and the right of our people to have their voices heard, yet we continue to see attacks on both.

That has been especially true as we confront a devastating Supreme Court decision that guts the Voting Rights Act and undermines protections against racial discrimination in our elections. As Justice Kagan warned in her dissent, the ruling gives states far greater leeway to dilute minority voting power "without legal consequence." At a moment when we should strengthen confidence in our democracy and expand participation, this Court continues moving in the [wrong direction](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mlnstuu3p22w&redir_log=942390022891446).

That is why Senate Democrats have continued to stand firm against efforts to undermine access to the ballot box, such as the so-called [SAVE America Act](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mhol7q43lc2q&redir_log=534334643006440) - a dangerous bill to make it harder for millions of American citizens to exercise their right to vote. Because Democrats held their ground, we've been able to block its passage in the Senate.

These fights are connected. Protecting the right to vote and defending democratic institutions go hand in hand with making government work better for the people we serve.

That's why I'm also looking towards what comes next: on how we lower costs, invest in our communities, and ensure the federal government is actually delivering for the people it serves.
### Delivering for Communities Across Maryland
Despite the dysfunction and chaos generated by the Trump Administration, I remain focused on delivering real results for communities across Maryland.

Recently, I joined local leaders in [Carroll County](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fnews%2fpress-releases%2fvan-hollen-olszewski-highlight-37-million-in-funding-secured-for-local-projects-across-carroll-county&redir_log=357643953271084) to announce more than $3.7 million in federal funding to support a range of projects that strengthen infrastructure, expand access to care, and build out our workforce.

In [Frederick County](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fnews%2fpress-releases%2fvan-hollen-alsobrooks-mcclain-delaney-secure-109-million-in-federal-funding-for-local-projects-in-frederick-county&redir_log=123172591441167), Senator Alsobrooks, Congresswoman McClain Delaney, and I announced $10.9 million secured in federal funding - including $3 million to support the new Frederick Youth Center and $1 million to renovate the Taney Avenue Senior Center and expand housing for senior residents.

In [Howard County](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fnews%2fpress-releases%2fvan-hollen-elfreth-highlight-over-6-million-in-federal-funding-secured-for-community-projects-in-howard-county&redir_log=012848360121148), I joined Congresswoman Elfreth and local leaders to tour the construction of the Artists Flats Project, a mixed-income housing development for which we secured $1.25 million in federal funding to expand housing options for low and moderate-income families. We also announced over $5 million in funding for three other projects to support local infrastructure services and STEM education.

In Montgomery County, I joined [So What Else Food Rescue Bank](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fnews%2fpress-releases%2fvan-hollen-alsobrooks-secure-750000-in-federal-funding-for-food-rescue-bank&redir_log=83454746044880) for their sixth anniversary celebration, where we announced $750,000 in federal funding. This investment will expand their food rescue and distribution efforts for families who are struggling to put food on the table across Montgomery, Prince George's, and Frederick Counties, as well as Baltimore City.

In Baltimore, alongside Congressman Mfume, Congressman Olszewski, Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott, and local leaders, we announced more than $1.1 million to help expand [Baltimore's Group Violence Reduction Strategy](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fnews%2fpress-releases%2fvan-hollen-mfume-olszewski-highlight-nearly-12-million-in-federal-funding-to-support-gun-violence-reduction-in-baltimore&redir_log=012129873681216) into more neighborhoods. We've already seen this program help save lives and reduce violence in communities across Baltimore, and this investment will help build on that progress and make more neighborhoods safer.

And earlier this week, I was joined by Senator Alsobrooks and Congressman Ivey to announce more than $7 million in investments for community priorities in Prince George's County. This included investments in growing youth support services at the Latin American Youth Center, expanding arts education programs run by Joe's Movement Emporium, upgrading the Attick Towers Apartments, and fostering local nonprofits at Ivy Community Charities.
### Thank You
Recently, I had the special chance to speak with the [historic Artemis II crew](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mj5ixv7oqk2w&redir_log=964763711161446) while they were in space. I asked Commander Reid Wiseman - a Maryland native and graduate of Dulaney High School in Baltimore County - what advice he would give to young people hoping to follow in his footsteps. His answer was simple: expand your horizons, take risks, and keep trying even if you can't get it right the first time, because learning how to fail can be the key to success.

Even amid all the challenges we are facing, moments like this are a reminder of what's possible when we invest in our future and direct resources towards the next generation.

There is no shortage of urgent work ahead, but I remain focused on the same core responsibility: standing up for Marylanders, protecting our democracy and our constitutional rights, and pushing back hard against the headwinds whipped up by the Trump Administration so we can make life more affordable for every American.

I am grateful to everyone across the state who continues to share their experiences, raise their voices, and stay engaged in this work. Your input directly shapes the fights we take on in the Senate and the solutions we continue to push forward.

Onwards,

Chris Van Hollen

To see more on my daily efforts to fight back against the Trump Administration, follow me on: [YouTube](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.youtube.com%2f%40senatorvanhollen&redir_log=49030338036296), [Bluesky](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov&redir_log=939838092693319), [Instagram](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.instagram.com%2fchrisvanhollen%3futm_source%3dig_web_button_share_sheet%26igsh%3dZDNlZDc0MzIxNw%253D%253D&redir_log=547268099313732), [Threads](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.threads.com%2f%40chrisvanhollen&redir_log=958032566321279), [Facebook](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.facebook.com%2fchrisvanhollen%2f&redir_log=328155479639284), and [X](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15711.61047877.7996980.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fx.com%2fChrisVanHollen&redir_log=218313979356198).

I know many Marylanders are both frustrated and angry by what they see coming out of Washington. I am too. Marylanders are also concerned about the struggles they are facing every day to make ends meet amidst rising costs. I am too. Those twin challenges are at the heart of the work I do every day in the Senate - from standing up to the Trump Administration's abuses of power to fighting to advance measures that strengthen economic opportunity and lower costs for working families. Here's the latest on all these fronts: Standing Up to Trump's Lawless Mass Deportation Agenda Republicans in Washington are once again making their priorities clear: instead of working to lower costs and make life more affordable for Americans, they are hellbent on providing a blank check for Trump's lawless ICE operations. Americans are struggling with skyrocketing prices on everything from gas to food costs because of Trump's illegal war in Iran, and people are facing steeper health care premiums after Republicans let ACA tax credits expire. Yet, instead of working with us to end this war and reduce costs, Senate Republicans used what's known as a bill to bypass normal Senate spending bill procedures in order to stuff an already bloated and out-of-control ICE operation with tens of billions more of taxpayers' dollars. This is on top of the record $75 billion - seven times higher than the normal annual amount - that Republicans gave to ICE last year, and despite the fact that tens of billions of dollars remain unspent as of the end of April. Last Thursday, we debated and voted all night in the Senate, where Republicans refused to support our efforts to rein in ICE misconduct and opposed over 20 amendments to stop this Administration's rampant abuses. Their stonewalling included blocking I offered with Senator Cassidy to make clear that Trump could not use his DOJ's proposed taxpayer-funded slush fund to provide payouts to January 6th insurrectionists and violent criminals. Instead, we required that those funds could be used ONLY to who were injured defending our Capitol on January 6th and members of their families who suffered harm as a result. Senate Republicans also blocked to prevent violent criminals and those who have committed crimes against children from receiving payouts from the Trump taxpayer slush fund. I made my position clear on this reckless bill once again: because - as I've said repeatedly - I will not support one more dime for a lawless ICE operation that refuses to make . Nevertheless, Senate Republicans voted to give ICE a blank check and, yesterday, House Republicans did the same thing. I've also been hearing directly from many of you about the real-life impacts of the Administration's cruel mass deportation agenda, including the ongoing pause on application processing at U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) that is disrupting people's ability to work, support their families, and plan for their futures. These impacts extend far beyond work authorizations and are affecting a wide range of applications, often with no clear exemptions or timelines. Please know that I hear you. I am actively engaged on these issues. I'm pressing the Administration for answers and relief - including urging to take immediate steps to resume the orderly processing of immigration and naturalization applications. While the recent that the government must restart asylum and immigration processing is a step in the right direction, we must keep fighting back. Your stories matter, and they are informing the work I'm doing every day in the Senate. Demanding Accountability from Todd Blanche, Kash Patel & Trump's Cronies As the Trump Administration pushes for massive spending at agencies like ICE, Congress has a responsibility to examine how taxpayer dollars are being used across the federal government - including at the Department of Justice and the FBI. That's why, as the lead Democrat of the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on Commerce, Justice, Science, and Related Agencies - which has jurisdiction over the Department of Justice and FBI funding - I recently used two hearings on the President's FY27 Budget Requests to press Trump Administration officials on corruption, abuses of power, and the politicization of law enforcement. During last month with Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche - who Trump has now nominated to be the Attorney General - I laid out examples of the horrible actions taken by the Trump DOJ. Blanche himself has been at the center of some of this Administration's most troubling scandals, from helping bury the Epstein files to overseeing a newly proposed $1.8 billion taxpayer-funded slush fund to provide payouts to Trump allies. During the hearing, I asked the Acting Attorney General if those who assaulted police officers on January 6th, and a pardoned January 6th rioter who was since convicted of molesting two children, would be eligible for payouts. . I am working to eliminate this fund outright. In the meantime, as discussed above, I on the Republican reconciliation bill to prevent anyone convicted of violent crimes or crimes against children from of your tax dollars. After the hearing, we also learned that, as part of this scheme to create the slush fund, Blanche also quietly to bar the IRS from ever reexamining Trump's, his family's, or his companies' prior taxes. This is unacceptable. While Blanche has more recently said he does not intend to proceed with the slush fund, all we have is his word to go on as Trump continues to say . Obviously, Blanche's word isn't good enough. What's more, he's confirmed the Trump family tax scheme still remains intact. I will not stop fighting back against both. I also pressed FBI Director Kash Patel about that his conduct and excessive drinking have interfered with his ability to perform his duties. I made clear: I don't give a damn what people do in their private lives, but when that conduct compromises their ability to protect and serve the American people, it's unacceptable. Patel responded by lashing out and making false statements and provable lies - while that it is a crime to lie to Congress. I also sought answers on his misuse of FBI resources - including diverting agents away from counterintelligence and violent crime investigations in order to pursue political vendettas and support Trump's mass deportation agenda. Both hearings reinforced the corrupt reality of this Administration: under Donald Trump, agencies that are supposed to protect the public and uphold the rule of law are increasingly being weaponized to do Trump's personal bidding. Every taxpayer dollar spent on political retaliation, corruption, or abuse is a dollar not being spent on keeping Americans safe or improving people's lives. I will continue using every tool available to demand transparency, expose abuses of power, and ensure that no Administration is above the law. Pushing Back Against Blank Checks for Endless Wars At the same time, I am fighting back against Trump's disastrous leadership on the global stage, as we are now over 100 days into the illegal war he and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu launched against Iran. Fourteen Americans have been killed and hundreds wounded. Thousands of civilians throughout the region have been killed. The Strait of Hormuz remains blocked, and remain high while keep going up. Trump revealed his views when : "I don't think about Americans' financial situation." Meanwhile, the Trump Administration admitted that it has spent $29 billion of your tax dollars on this war in just the first two months. At that rate, which was reportedly a lowball estimate, the costs would be over $40 billion as of today. When you are digging yourself into a hole, ! I have also pressed Secretary Hegseth for answers and after he dismantled key Department of Defense offices tasked with preventing civilian casualties, like the Tomahawk missile strike that killed over 120 Iranian school children. These safeguards exist for a reason: to protect innocent lives. Their removal raises urgent questions about compliance with U.S. and international law. But Secretary Hegseth dismissed those concerns and even said that the rules of engagement were "stupid" - rules designed to prevent innocent people from getting killed in war. I've gone to the many times to to support the eight War Powers Resolutions we've brought up to end this illegal war of choice and reclaim Congress's constitutional authority. And I've introduced my own War Powers Resolution as part of that effort, because the Constitution is clear: the power to declare war resides with Congress precisely because our Founding Fathers feared putting that power in the hands of one impulsive president. Meanwhile, Trump and his Administration are openly musing about yet another illegal, unauthorized military intervention, this time in Cuba, as I spoke about on the . It's failures like these that are hurting Americans at home and hurting our stature abroad. When Secretary Rubio appeared recently before the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, I laid out some of these failures . Instead of taking responsibility for these disastrous policies, ending the war in Iran, or reversing course in Cuba, Rubio, Hegseth, and the Trump Administration are asking Congress to approve a in Pentagon spending. After pushing through a $1 trillion defense budget last year, they are proposing nearly $500 billion more - bringing total military spending to roughly $1.5 trillion. I will not provide one more dime for the illegal war against Iran, and I will not support a bloated Pentagon budget - because that is not what is best for the people of the United States. I will continue to stand up for the Constitution, demand accountability, and focus on the priorities that matter to the American people. Defending Our Democracy and the Right to Vote The strength of our democracy depends on both the rule of law and the right of our people to have their voices heard, yet we continue to see attacks on both. That has been especially true as we confront a devastating Supreme Court decision that guts the Voting Rights Act and undermines protections against racial discrimination in our elections. As Justice Kagan warned in her dissent, the ruling gives states far greater leeway to dilute minority voting power "without legal consequence." At a moment when we should strengthen confidence in our democracy and expand participation, this Court continues moving in the . That is why Senate Democrats have continued to stand firm against efforts to undermine access to the ballot box, such as the so-called - a dangerous bill to make it harder for millions of American citizens to exercise their right to vote. Because Democrats held their ground, we've been able to block its passage in the Senate. These fights are connected. Protecting the right to vote and defending democratic institutions go hand in hand with making government work better for the people we serve. That's why I'm also looking towards what comes next: on how we lower costs, invest in our communities, and ensure the federal government is actually delivering for the people it serves. Delivering for Communities Across Maryland Despite the dysfunction and chaos generated by the Trump Administration, I remain focused on delivering real results for communities across Maryland. Recently, I joined local leaders in to announce more than $3.7 million in federal funding to support a range of projects that strengthen infrastructure, expand access to care, and build out our workforce. In , Senator Alsobrooks, Congresswoman McClain Delaney, and I announced $10.9 million secured in federal funding - including $3 million to support the new Frederick Youth Center and $1 million to renovate the Taney Avenue Senior Center and expand housing for senior residents. In , I joined Congresswoman Elfreth and local leaders to tour the construction of the Artists Flats Project, a mixed-income housing development for which we secured $1.25 million in federal funding to expand housing options for low and moderate-income families. We also announced over $5 million in funding for three other projects to support local infrastructure services and STEM education. In Montgomery County, I joined for their sixth anniversary celebration, where we announced $750,000 in federal funding. This investment will expand their food rescue and distribution efforts for families who are struggling to put food on the table across Montgomery, Prince George's, and Frederick Counties, as well as Baltimore City. In Baltimore, alongside Congressman Mfume, Congressman Olszewski, Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott, and local leaders, we announced more than $1.1 million to help expand into more neighborhoods. We've already seen this program help save lives and reduce violence in communities across Baltimore, and this investment will help build on that progress and make more neighborhoods safer. And earlier this week, I was joined by Senator Alsobrooks and Congressman Ivey to announce more than $7 million in investments for community priorities in Prince George's County. This included investments in growing youth support services at the Latin American Youth Center, expanding arts education programs run by Joe's Movement Emporium, upgrading the Attick Towers Apartments, and fostering local nonprofits at Ivy Community Charities. Thank You Recently, I had the special chance to speak with the while they were in space. I asked Commander Reid Wiseman - a Maryland native and graduate of Dulaney High School in Baltimore County - what advice he would give to young people hoping to follow in his footsteps. His answer was simple: expand your horizons, take risks, and keep trying even if you can't get it right the first time, because learning how to fail can be the key to success. Even amid all the challenges we are facing, moments like this are a reminder of what's possible when we invest in our future and direct resources towards the next generation. There is no shortage of urgent work ahead, but I remain focused on the same core responsibility: standing up for Marylanders, protecting our democracy and our constitutional rights, and pushing back hard against the headwinds whipped up by the Trump Administration so we can make life more affordable for every American. I am grateful to everyone across the state who continues to share their experiences, raise their voices, and stay engaged in this work. Your input directly shapes the fights we take on in the Senate and the solutions we continue to push forward. Onwards, Chris Van Hollen To see more on my daily efforts to fight back against the Trump Administration, follow me on: , , , , , and . |

And I’m humbled by all the amazing supporters who invested in our campaign to make it happen. But to win the primary, we risked everything and spent down to zero. That means to win this race we’re relying on grassroots donors like you to help us immediately refill our campaign coffers. = | = I’ll level with you, Peter: Even though Democrats' path to the Senate majority rolls through Iowa, we’re still underdogs in this must-win race. A big part of that is money. My Republican opponent Ashley Hinson has taken millions from corporate PACs, so she entered the General Election with over $6 million in the bank. And that’s before the shady dark money Republican Super PACs spend their $40 million warchest. But the thing is, I’m no stranger to tough fights. I wasn’t supposed to win my Iowa State House races. I went door to door, crawling up stairs, dragging my wheelchair after me to talk to voters face-to-face. That’s how I won a deep-red Trump district.Twice. If I had time in this campaign to drag myself up to every front porch in Iowa, believe me, I would. But I don’t. The only way we can win is to keep getting our message out on airwaves across Iowa. And to do that, we need money. Today. Not in a month or even two weeks. **The best thing about this campaign is the people. **

From Cincinnati to Cleveland, Guernsey County to Toledo, I love meeting folks all across Ohio and hearing their stories.
That’s what public service is all about.

It’s about knowing the folks you represent, understanding their toughest days, and then fighting like hell to make things better. If you agree, **[will you chip in whatever you can to help us flip this battleground seat in Ohio?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133055015/626588991/-642432923?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&amount=5&refcode=jtk4889-fr-ndva&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3NTU5NzdkNC1kNjY0LWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=A45jIkkzssG3F6fvEn-lhlCO25ebDSrBZXZjtjxA-xc=)**

The **dad in Warren** who works full time but can't afford groceries for his family.

The **retiree in Akron** praying their Social Security doesn't get cut.

The **worker in Dayton** who’s doing everything right but still can't get a raise.

The **farmer in Darke County** getting squeezed by rising fuel and fertilizer prices.

**The nurse, the teacher, the truck driver, the factory worker – the hardworking folks across Ohio who bust their tails every day but can't get ahead because the system is rigged.**
These Ohioans deserve a senator who will fight for them – not for billionaire donors, not for corporate lobbyists, and not for the Washington insiders.

**Kristina Knickerbocker** , running to flip Ohio’s 10th Congressional District, is an Air Force veteran and nurse who worked multiple jobs to put herself through school.

clean_body: | = We knew that would get your attention. Now, Peter, let us introduce you to a few women who should have it instead. Women who are veterans. Women who have working-class backgrounds. Women who are caregivers, small business owners, public servants, and leaders. They know what it means to stretch a dollar, make hard choices, serve their communities, and fight for the people counting on them. That is not just a compelling biography. It is a strong electoral strategy. Democrats need candidates who can speak directly to voters who feel ignored, squeezed, and written off. = | = Kristina Knickerbocker , running to flip Ohio’s 10th Congressional District, is an Air Force veteran and nurse who worked multiple jobs to put herself through school. Sarah Trone Garriott , running to flip Iowa’s 3rd Congressional District, is a minister, a mom, and the daughter of a nurse and an auto mechanic who worked at Walmart, waited tables, and cleaned hotel rooms to pay for college. Kaela Berg , running for Minnesota’s 2nd Congressional District, is a union flight attendant who has worked multiple jobs at once. Rebecca Cooke , running to flip Wisconsin’s 3rd Congressional District, is a longtime waitress and daughter of dairy farmers who still takes diner shifts between campaign stops. Keisha Lance Bottoms , running to flip the Georgia governor’s office, is a fifth-generation Georgian, mom of four, and former Atlanta mayor who is fighting to lower costs and deliver for working families across Georgia. Deb Haaland , running for governor of New Mexico, is a single mom who relied on food stamps and sold homemade salsa to make ends meet while raising her daughter. And then there are the badass women who have already served their country in uniform — and are now stepping up to keep serving in office: JoAnna Mendoza , running to flip Arizona’s 6th Congressional District, served in the Navy and Marine Corps. Rebecca Bennett , running to flip New Jersey’s 7th Congressional District, is a former Navy helicopter pilot. Jessica Killin , running to flip Colorado’s 5th Congressional District, served as an Army captain and paratrooper. Leela Gray , running to flip Florida’s 13th Congressional District, is a retired Army brigadier general. Nancy Lacore , running to flip South Carolina's 1st Congressional District, worked her way through the Naval ranks to eventually serve as the Chief of the Navy Reserve, entrusted to lead more than 60,000 sailors. These women have served their country. They have worked for a paycheck. They have cared for their families and communities. And now, they are running to represent people whose lives reflect the same struggles they’ve experienced firsthand. This is why electing women matters so much this cycle, Peter. The women EMILYs List supports are not running because politics is easy. They are running because their communities need leaders who understand what working families are actually up against — and who are ready to fight for them. President Donald Trump announced Wednesday he is preparing to order new strikes targeting Iranian power plants and bridges, **[telling Fox News](https://substack.com/redirect/b050fb0b-feb1-412b-a5f9-1ccab341ffc4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** the country has taken too long to reach a negotiated settlement. On Truth Social, Trump declared Iran's military is in ruins -- its navy and air force largely destroyed -- and warned the country would "have to pay the price" for stalling diplomacy.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b050fb0b-feb1-412b-a5f9-1ccab341ffc4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **The escalating threats follow a rapid exchange of military strikes.** After Iran shot down a US Apache helicopter near the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, Washington launched retaliatory "self-defense strikes" Tuesday evening. Iran responded Wednesday morning by targeting American military installations in Bahrain, Jordan, and Kuwait with drones and missiles.
* **The flare-up marks a sharp reversal in tone.** As recently as Tuesday, Trump had described nuclear negotiations with Tehran as being in their "final throes," suggesting a deal could materialize within days. That optimism has now given way to explicit threats of further infrastructure strikes.

* * *
# **Trump-Backed Hilton Advances to California Governor 's Race**
Conservative candidate Steve Hilton, endorsed by President Donald Trump, **[secured second place](https://substack.com/redirect/91eabc3e-2e11-458f-8796-4135cf05ccf5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in California's open gubernatorial primary with roughly 25% of the vote, narrowly trailing former Biden HHS Secretary Xavier Becerra's 28%. The two will meet in the November general election after Hilton edged out billionaire Democrat Tom Steyer, who finished just behind him. The AP called the race Tuesday, a full week after Election Day.

| | |
---
| | | |
# RUNOFF ALERT!
---
| Friends, **Last night, thanks to your support, our campaign advanced to the Republican runoff for Congress on June 23.** I am incredibly grateful to every volunteer who knocked doors, every supporter who put out a yard sign, every donor who invested in our campaign, and every voter who placed their trust in me. When we launched this campaign nearly a year ago, we made a commitment to put the Lowcountry first. Since then, we've attended hundreds of events, met with thousands of voters, and traveled every corner of the district listening to your concerns and sharing our vision for the future. **Now, we have two more weeks to finish the job.** Over the coming days, you'll hear a lot about my record and the _clear choice_ facing Republican voters in this runoff. This race is about more than personalities or campaign slogans. **This runoff is a choice between a conservative who has delivered results and a candidate trying to reinvent their record.** As your State Representative, I've cut taxes, secured critical infrastructure funding, fought government waste, defended our conservative values, and worked every day to make life more affordable for Lowcountry families. **I am asking for your vote one more time on June 23.** Together, let's keep fighting for the Lowcountry and ensure our next Congressman is a conservative who has delivered results. Thank you for your continued support. Sincerely, Mark Smith
---

If Donald Trump gets his way...

* The USPS will be able to ship guns through the mail.
* Gun stores would get a free pass even if they violate the law.

They know that these rule changes will increase the risk of mass shootings and make it harder for law enforcement to do their job.
But they’re doing it anyway. Because the only thing that matters to them is helping their friends in the gun industry profit.

name: Raja Krishnamoorthi
subject: My next chapter…
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
Team, over the last few months, I've had some time to think.
And the more I thought, the more I kept coming back to something my father used to say at the dinner table when I was growing up in Peoria.
He'd look at us and say: "Think of the greatness of this country. Whatever you do, make sure this country is there for the next families who need it."
He said that as an immigrant who came here with nothing. He said it after our family had struggled, having lived in public housing and on food stamps. He said it because he believed — with everything he had — that this country could still be a place where hard work leads somewhere. Where a kid with a hard-to-pronounce name still gets a real shot.
I built my entire life around that belief.
And right now, that belief is under direct attack.
Donald Trump and his MAGA allies are gutting the safety net that kept my family afloat.
They're rigging the economy for billionaires while working and middle-class families fall further behind.
They're weaponizing the government against immigrants, against workers, against anyone who dares to believe the American Dream should be available to everyone — not just the powerful and well-connected.
My father's America is being dismantled piece by piece. And I refuse to sit back and watch it happen.
That's why today, I'm launching Equal Opportunity Now (formerly known as RAJAPAC) — a group dedicated to supporting causes and leaders who will fight like hell to expand opportunity, take on Trump's MAGA agenda, and make sure this country is still there for the next families that need it.
Equal Opportunity Now will support the fights that matter most to working families: making sure every child has food on the table and access to a quality education, lowering prescription drug costs and grocery prices, strengthening good-paying jobs and workers' rights, holding corporate bad actors and corrupt politicians accountable, and fighting bigotry and prejudice in all its forms.
These problems require ambitious, bold solutions, championed by leaders who know that our time is running out.
That's why I need you to become a founding donor of Equal Opportunity Now today.
The leaders and groups who are willing to fight back against Trump's MAGA agenda and deliver real change are out there. But they need funding, infrastructure, and people ready to invest in them early. Founding donors who step up now make it possible. They make it real.
Will you chip in $25, $50, or whatever you can to become a founding donor of Equal Opportunity Now before midnight tonight? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
DONATE TODAY TO BECOME A FOUNDING DONOR! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
My father was right about this country. It's worth fighting for.
Thanks for joining me in the next chapter of my journey; it means the world to me.
— Raja Krishnamoorthi
Founder | Equal Opportunity Now
Visit Our Website To Learn More! [https://www.equalopportunitynow.org/]

Equal Opportunity Now is d/b/a Reviving American Jobs PAC (RAJA PAC)

Anti-abortion extremists haven't just created a reproductive health crisis; they've created a legal one. A patchwork of contradictory state laws is leaving patients without care and providers afraid to act. It's not just unjust. [It's putting lives at risk.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/133060754/626607658/-1451183686?sourceid=1151403&utm_campaign=26emige-0608aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=liz&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzY2RjMjg4NC1kZDY0LWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=eK6nAuP5LkiBgz9i2C0XqTa9QcVRRr4wR7eu_v3OQb8=&emci=aa934080-0d61-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&emdi=3cdc2884-dd64-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&ceid=954237) | [FIGHT BACK WITH US](https://click.everyaction.com/k/133060755/626607659/-1451183686?sourceid=1151403&utm_campaign=26emige-0608aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=liz&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzY2RjMjg4NC1kZDY0LWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=eK6nAuP5LkiBgz9i2C0XqTa9QcVRRr4wR7eu_v3OQb8=&emci=aa934080-0d61-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&emdi=3cdc2884-dd64-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&ceid=954237)

Here’s what you need to know right now about the legal state of reproductive rights in the U.S. today:
* **Ambiguity is a weapon.** Anti-abortion laws are often written vaguely—sometimes deliberately—to sow fear, create confusion, and give extremists new tools to punish patients and providers alike.
* **State bans are going national.** Laws like South Carolina 4760 are designed to reach beyond state lines, limiting access to medication abortion more than ever. The goal: intimidate doctors and erode abortion access everywhere, even in states where rights are still protected.
* **Medication abortion remains under siege.** Mifepristone is used in more than 60% of U.S. abortions. The Supreme Court recently paused the latest effort to restrict it but make no mistake: that's a delay, not a victory. The attacks are not stopping.

This is a hard moment. There's no pretending otherwise. But when I think about the brave plaintiffs who have taken on unjust laws head-on—and when I think about the [people behind us who refuse to give up](https://click.everyaction.com/k/133060756/626607660/-1451183686?sourceid=1151403&utm_campaign=26emige-0608aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=liz&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzY2RjMjg4NC1kZDY0LWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=eK6nAuP5LkiBgz9i2C0XqTa9QcVRRr4wR7eu_v3OQb8=&emci=aa934080-0d61-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&emdi=3cdc2884-dd64-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&ceid=954237)—I have hope.

Thank you for being in this fight.

Onward,

Liz Wagner

subject: Statement Regarding Yesterday’s Primary Election Outcome
body:
| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/ZPTzyb2AaiW?e=5d7176e969&c2id=0715660f99493bd2d61bdbd7e3d6dd36)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
Friends,Below is a copy of David’s statement/social media post regarding the outcome of yesterday’s US Senate primary election:
“Well, we did surprise a bit, given we were outspent by our opponents (by Graham Platner 682 to 1 - $15 million to $22 thousand and Governor Mills’s 227 to 1 - $5 million to $22 thousand) and largely ignored/dismissed by the press... I am allowed to vent a little. Our 8% to 9% of the vote is considerably more than the 1% to 3% unfailingly forecasted by the pundits and press, but nowhere near the percentage required to win. So, congratulations to Graham and his campaign, and a big, big THANK YOU to the Mainers who supported our efforts! We gave it a go and will continue to make the case that to strengthen our democracy and address our most pressing challenges we need to remove money from our politics and substantially reform our governing practices and institutions.And here’s hoping that Maine’s most famous Oyster farmer can keep it up and defeat Maine’s often concerned, yet never sufficiently concerned, Senator Susan Collins in November...”Thank very much for your and best always,Team Costello

Peter,
I can't thank you enough.
I am beyond grateful for your support. It is the fuel that keeps our campaign moving.
I wake up every morning driven by a single purpose: making a real difference in your life and protecting the values we hold dear in Maine.
When I made the decision to run, I knew the attacks would be relentless. I am confident in my decision because I know I am not standing alone.

Sincerely,

Education and the arts have been under constant attack by this current administration. And after hosting Reading Rainbow for more than 20 years on PBS, I was devastated to see federal funding for public broadcasting completely decimated.

name: Small Town PAC
subject: The 3 things we need to win
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Small Town PAC, [smalltownpac
body:
Show up early. Talk about what matters. Back leaders people know and trust.
#
Peter,
If Democrats want to start winning again and expand the map, the work is pretty straightforward:
**1\. Show up early — and stay.**
When Democrats stop showing up in certain places, somebody else fills the void.
Too often, it is people who have no real interest in helping working families — just dividing them, distracting them, and cashing in while communities get left behind.
**2\. Talk about what people actually feel.**
Strong schools. Good jobs. Healthcare. Child care. The family farm. Main Street businesses. Whether your kids can afford to build a life in the place they grew up.
That is what people are talking about around kitchen tables, in break rooms, and at Friday night football games. Democrats have to make the case on the issues that actually impact people’s lives.
**3\. Back leaders who know their communities.**
That means finding and supporting teachers, nurses, veterans, laborers, small business owners, and young people who understand what their neighbors are up against — and who are ready to fight for the places they call home.
_That is what Small Town PAC is built to do._ We are going to help Democrats compete in more places, support leaders who actually know their communities, and make the case everywhere.

See link below)_ **Please join us in congratulating [Jimmy Kimmel on winning a prestigious Peabody award](https://default.salsalabs.org/T7c38cbf3-7d36-49c8-8673-fad360567ec1/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)[!](https://default.salsalabs.org/T825c7f4f-aeb6-4a99-8154-844f64bdbc8c/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)** _" Jimmy Kimmel Live! was announced as a winner of the award ... after facing what Peabody described as an "unprecedented" attack from the Trump administration and unsuccessful attempts to have the show completely taken off the air."_ **And thank him for using the occasion to [remind](https://default.salsalabs.org/T01173a53-65d2-4f43-b62a-7a1517528148/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) the world what a horse's ass Trump is**. _" I called our president Fattyshack," Kimmel said, before listing other nicknames he has given the 79-year-old president over the years. ---
Peter, I’m running because I want my daughters to inherit a country with honest government, real opportunity, and a future worth fighting for. That is why I stepped into this race. It is why I’ve spent years rooting out corruption, fixing budgets, and making Scranton work for real people instead of cronies. When I was on the school board and the auditor general’s team, I saw what happens when public trust is broken. I ran for mayor to change that. We cleaned up City Hall, balanced the books, cut red tape, and brought small businesses and homes back to our neighborhoods. I did that as a mom, and I did it because I want my kids to know that government can work for them, not profit from them. Congress is where this fight matters next. Hey folks,
This one got spicy.
**Adam Mockler** joined me for a conversation that started with Republican attacks on Democrats and quickly turned into something bigger: what strength actually looks like in politics, why MAGA influencers keep obsessing over masculinity, and how Republicans are trying to distract voters from their own scandals. We got personal. We got blunt. And we didn't hold back.
**Here 's what we got into:**
* [**00:01:07**] Trump shows up to a Knicks playoff game, gets booed, and the conversation turns into a surprisingly revealing look at how MAGA makes everything about one person.
* [**00:08:18**] We break down what masculinity actually means--protecting, providing, showing up for the people you love--and why so many right-wing personalities seem terrified of that definition.
* [**00:15:35**] A deeper conversation about Tucker Carlson, election lies, and why integrity matters more than performative toughness.
* [**00:24:25**] We walk through the long list of allegations and scandals surrounding Ken Paxton and ask a simple question: why are the loudest moralizers always asking for exceptions?
* [**00:33:01**] The conversation shifts to the Maine Senate race, political accountability, redemption, and the stakes of winning back power in a moment when democracy is still on the line.

At its heart, this conversation is about what kind of people we want leading this country. We talk about the the attacks on James Talarico, the growing role of AI-generated political propaganda, the challenge Democrats face with young men, and the reality that voters are hungry for something more authentic than culture-war theatrics. If you care about where this country is headed--and how we build a politics rooted in responsibility instead of outrage--this conversation is essential listening. I’ll be honest, Derek: I don’t love dress shoes. Of course, I’ll wear them when the moment calls for it. But when I’m out on the trail, meeting Pennsylvanians at their workplaces, their homes, and their communities? I’d rather put on a pair of sneakers every time _._ _[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133069131/626632811/1075131337?refcode=email_061026_sneakers&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NTY5MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjOTIwY2VhMS1lNjY0LWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=cRIkE8zqqW1eCRn5EEOu-d8zOP6OrMsB3QEF2tjDKvg=)__Pretty nice kicks, huh?_ Here’s the deal: I’ve put a whole lot of miles on my newest pair of sneakers since Launch Day. Enough to the point where... they’re not looking so squeaky clean anymore. But Derek, I think that’s a damn good metaphor for our campaign. In Pennsylvania, progress doesn’t always come easy. It takes hard work, common sense, and yes, compromise to get things done. It’s not always the prettiest process — but once you brush off the dust, I’ll tell you this: **It gets the job done.** [**Derek,****I’m more than willing to get my hands (and my shoes) a little dirty to get sh*t done for Pennsylvania. If that’s the kind of leadership you want to see in our government, I’m humbly asking for your support. name: Melat Kiros
subject: The Sun Will Rise: Who's afraid of Melat Kiros?
body:
Dark money can't drown out a movement built by the people.
| |
---
| | | |
---
## **Who's afraid of Melat Kiros?**
Someone just dropped $350,000 to make sure you don't hear about this race. Monday, a group calling itself the "Mile High Accountability Project" filed a 24-hour notice with the FEC — the kind you have to file when big money moves fast. Three hundred and fifty thousand dollars, all of it going to digital advertising in support of Diana DeGette, the 30-year incumbent we're running against. The payee is a firm in Washington, DC. The funder? Unknown.
| |
---
| We don't know who the Mile High Accountability Project is. That's by design. Super PACs like this one aren't required to say. They can take unlimited money from corporations, billionaires, and special interest groups — and they can spend it without telling you where it came from _until after the election_.
---
| | What we do know: it's not coming from Denver. It is not coming from the families in this district who are one missed paycheck from losing their housing. It's not coming from the parents paying more for childcare than rent. It's not coming from anyone who has stood in line at a food bank, or gone without insurance, or watched their neighborhood change while their wages stayed flat. $350,000 doesn't come from people like that.
---
| | It comes from people who have a lot to lose if Denver sends a different kind of representative to Washington.
---
| [](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/NRDnZF60m5svYxfS2rWGXrtmQgGVYvpS/click?signature=5a2b1318462380b501946e229b59b10b7037bc83&url=https%3A%2F%2Fx.com%2Fryangrim%2Fstatus%2F2064053774185013318%3Fs%3D20)
---
| | This race is simple at its core. On one side: a 30-year incumbent backed by a mysterious super PAC, spending like it has something to protect. On the other: a people-powered campaign that doesn't take corporate PAC money, period. A campaign endorsed by Justice Democrats. One of only three national DSA endorsements in 2026. And [endorsed by many more](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/NRDnZF60m5svYxfS2rWGXrtmQgGVYvpS/click?signature=48f7712f134549aa7dae4a49e692c8e2fb0480ff&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.kirosforco.com%2Fendorsements). Medicare for All. Housing First. Universal Childcare. An arms embargo. Real diplomacy instead of endless war. That's what I am running on, and every dollar this campaign raises comes from people in this district who believe it's possible. Together, we have knocked on doors, picked up the phones, staked out our local farmers markets, art walks, and pride events, and had real conversations with over 60,000 people across CO-1. Not megadonors. Not power brokers. Neighbors. Together, we are going to show that $350,000 in dark money can't drown out a movement built by the people it's actually trying to reach. Twenty days left.
---
|
---

Rally with Melat Kiros and Hasan Piker **
| | [](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/NRDnZF60m5svYxfS2rWGXrtmQgGVYvpS/click?signature=9060daada534122dd4f10570234b5213a365a1e4&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwin.kirosforco.com%2Frally)

A _new_ generation of leaders is showing up for working people, unapologetically and unbought. On Sunday, June 14th, Congressional candidates Melat Kiros, Julie Gonzales, Justin Pearson, and Donavan McKinney will join Hasan Piker for a rally in Denver ahead of Colorado’s June 30th primary election.
---
| | We are done waiting for change and ready to fight for it: Medicare for All, immigrant dignity, affordable housing, and an end to the big-money politics that's rigged the system against working families.

## **_I’m reading_ :
Bernie Sanders and a 50% public stake in AI**
| | [](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/NRDnZF60m5svYxfS2rWGXrtmQgGVYvpS/click?signature=b21a584478d124072efe60309d6f25f1bc3d3c49&url=https%3A%2F%2Fthehill.com%2Fpolicy%2Ftechnology%2F5906140-sanders-ai-ownership-wealth%2F)
---
| I’m so excited about the prospect of Senator Sanders’ plan to introduce a bill “proposing to give the public a 50 percent stake in large artificial intelligence (AI) companies.” I will support it from my first day in Congress, for the same two reasons cited by Senator Sanders:
---
| | “First, it would give the American people a direct role in determining the future of this technology. No longer would the future of AI be dictated by a handful of Big Tech oligarchs, while the rest of the world sits back and watches them do what they want. “Secondly, it would guarantee that the trillions of dollars potentially generated by AI are used to improve the lives of all of us — not simply to make the richest people on Earth even richer.” [Read more at The Hill](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/NRDnZF60m5svYxfS2rWGXrtmQgGVYvpS/click?signature=b21a584478d124072efe60309d6f25f1bc3d3c49&url=https%3A%2F%2Fthehill.com%2Fpolicy%2Ftechnology%2F5906140-sanders-ai-ownership-wealth%2F)

Donald Trump is using the United States Postal Service to strong-arm Democratic states into surrendering their voter lists. The threat is simple: hand over the data, or your voters' ballots do not get delivered. And those lists contain the names and home addresses of every registered Democrat in those states.
We know exactly what MAGA does with voter data. In 2021, a dark money group called True the Vote challenged more than 364,000 Georgia voters just before the Senate runoff that handed Democrats the majority. Young voters and Black voters were twice as likely to be challenged, the same voters who flipped Georgia in 2020. A federal judge later ruled their data "utterly lacked credibility" and "verged on reckless."

clean_body: Donald Trump is using the United States Postal Service to strong-arm Democratic states into surrendering their voter lists. The data pipeline is being established right now to rig the upcoming midterm | | | | | == | Peter, A little over a week ago, it was revealed that the U.S. Postal Service is moving forward with a plan to limit mail-in voting by only sending ballots to voters who are registered on a list approved by the federal government. Now there is an even more alarming update: | == Donald Trump is using the United States Postal Service to strong-arm Democratic states into surrendering their voter lists. The threat is simple: hand over the data, or your voters' ballots do not get delivered. And those lists contain the names and home addresses of every registered Democrat in those states. We know exactly what MAGA does with voter data. In 2021, a dark money group called True the Vote challenged more than 364,000 Georgia voters just before the Senate runoff that handed Democrats the majority. Young voters and Black voters were twice as likely to be challenged, the same voters who flipped Georgia in 2020. A federal judge later ruled their data "utterly lacked credibility" and "verged on reckless." But getting caught does not stop dark money operations, it just sends them shopping for better data. There is no better data than official government voter records and Trump is delivering it. In April, it was revealed the Trump admin is secretly funneling seized voter data to political groups with a track record of trying to overturn election results: | == The data pipeline is being established right now to rig the upcoming midterm elections. Trump uses the USPS to squeeze the states, the lists flow to dark money groups, and those groups mass-challenge Democratic voters off the rolls before the most important midterm of our lives. Legal challenges to this rule are coming, and they will land right where MAGA wants them: The U.S. Supreme Court. We have all seen how this Court rules. They overturned Roe. They gutted the Voting Rights Act. They handed Trump criminal immunity. This court has been fully exposed as a puppet of Trump and MAGA extremists, willing to torch a half-century of precedent to tilt elections their way. So ask yourself: do you trust this Supreme Court to stop Trump from weaponizing voter data against Democrats? Neither do we. This is exactly why Defend Our Courts exists. We are fighting on two fronts. First, building a firewall of state Supreme Courts with the power to protect free and fair elections state by state. body:
America is a nation of immigrants, and nothing Republicans have to say will change that.
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=2266%2E791427%2EHaM99f)
[](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-jun26.ltbpUI&refcode=em260610-1-subs&t=2&akid=2266%2E791427%2EHaM99f)
Friend, we’ve all heard the slogan “America is a nation of immigrants.”
And it’s true — there is no America without immigration, from the original British colonies, to the founding of the United States, to today.
**If Republicans like Trump and Nancy Mace think you have to be born in the states to be a ‘real American,’ then they simply don’t understand our history.**
Alexander Hamilton was born in Saint Kitts and Nevis, but that didn’t stop him from fighting for American independence, serving as the first Treasury Secretary, and getting his face on the $10 bill.
Joseph Pulitzer was born in Hungary, but is regarded as one of the most important newspaper publishers in American history, with the most prestigious award for journalism still carrying his name.
Renowned thinkers and inventors like Alexander Graham Bell, Nikola Tesla, and Albert Einstein were all born abroad, but came to America to advance their fields and contribute to America’s scientific prowess.
And it would take an entire second email to list every famous immigrant business leader, athlete, actor, writer, or musician who has contributed so greatly to American life, from the Warner Brothers to Rihanna.
Those famous names coincide with millions of immigrants who made America what it is today; immigrants who built railroads to connect our country, plowed fields to feed their fellow Americans, worked in factories during our industrial boom, and chipped in to our great melting pot through art, music, food, language, traditions, and new ideas.
**America is a nation of immigrants, and nothing Republicans have to say will change that.**
There are currently 19 members of Congress who immigrated to the United States, including Ilhan Omar. Our movement fights for their right — whether Democrat or Republican — to represent their communities and be part of the work to improve and govern America. We don’t care what Nancy Mace thinks.
[**If you agree that people like Ilhan Omar are what make America great, chip in to our campaign today. With immigrant communities under constant attack, especially here in Minnesota, we need strong leaders like Ilhan more than ever. We’re halfway there. Will you send your letter today? | | | Hey Peter, The 14th anniversary of DACA is coming up in just a few days on Monday, June 15. You would think that after this many years of building our entire lives and careers here, our communities would have the safety and stability we need. Unfortunately, we’re facing the most dangerous moment in DACA’s history. Without a pathway to citizenship, DACA recipients and millions of immigrants continue to face uncertainty about their future in the country they call home. From unprecedented DACA renewal delays to attacks on TPS and birthright citizenship, our families are living through a nightmare as programs meant to protect us are being dismantled before our eyes. From now until June 15, we plan to send 30,000 letters to our members of Congress calling on them to stop the delegalization agenda and deliver citizenship to millions of our neighbors. With only 5 days to go, all of us must unite to meet this goal. Peter - From California to Wisconsin to Connecticut, young people are gathering around the country to write and hand-deliver letters to their members of Congress ahead of June 15th. In California, professors are bringing their students together in the classroom while others are gathering on Twitch to write letters from the comfort of their own homes. In Washington State, allies tabled at a local multicultural festival where their neighbors could stop by to write their letter. While young people in Michigan, Louisiana and Florida are hosting Community Meetings to write letters to Congress. When each one of us contributes something, we’re able to achieve the unimaginable. Now, it's your turn and you can send a digital letter right now! In power, Nico and the UWD team | Follow us on: | | | | |

Inside our office, tables are covered in supplies and open boxes. Coworkers are coming together, packing materials, sealing kits, and sending them out the door as fast as possible.

_Above: Activism kits bound for new chapters being packed with Constitutions, chapter handbooks, American flags, and more at TPUSA HQ in Arizona_
---
These boxes aren't sitting around waiting for someone to need them.

They're already claimed. And we don't have extras.

By the time one batch goes out, more requests come in.

Different schools, different students, same situation -- they want to start something, and they're asking us to help them do it.

That's where things stand right now.

We have more students stepping up than we can fully support at the moment.

And I don't say that lightly.

Because for years, the challenge wasn't getting students the tools -- it was getting them to speak up at all. Most kept their heads down.

The Left has spent years trying to convince this generation to sit down, stay quiet, and be ashamed of their country and everything that makes it great.

And for a long time, it worked. But that's all changing.

Now, we're seeing students stand up and push back.

**We saw it clearly at Wheeling High School in the Chicago suburbs -- Charlie's alma mater. **

For the first time, students there launched a Club America chapter. It took months to get approved, but a chapter is finally there.

And now, students are standing outside with signs about free markets and freedom -- not because it's easy, but because they've decided it matters more than staying quiet.

That's not something you can just manufacture. But it is something you can support when it happens.

And it's not isolated growth anymore.

**We 're now working with more than 1,450 college chapters and over 3,400 high school chapters across the country. That's real scale. **

But if you zoom out, there are roughly 27,000 high schools in America.

That means tens of thousands of campuses where the Left still dominates the conversation...

And where students are waiting for someone to help them stand up and speak.

So as much as this has grown, we're still in the early innings of what Charlie actually set out to build.

What's different now is the pace.

**Many states are moving to bring Club America chapters to every high school statewide, including: **

✅ Arkansas
✅ Florida
✅ Idaho
✅ Indiana
✅ Montana
✅ Nebraska
✅ Oklahoma
✅ South Carolina
✅ Texas
✅ Tennessee

That brings us to ten states now taking this seriously -- not just talk, but action.
