It’s Joey here. Happy Pride Month! As a member of the Arizona LGBTQ+ community, I know that Pride is about celebration, but it is also about courage, visibility, and the generations of people who fought to make it possible for us to live openly and honestly. And right now, that fight is far from over. We still need your courage. Across the country, LGBTQ+ people are being targeted by politicians who want to roll back our rights, erase our stories, and make life harder for kids, families, workers, and neighbors who simply want to live with dignity. Here in Arizona, we’ve seen what happens when extremists gain power. But we also know what happens when Democrats win. Arizona Democrats are standing up for our rights:
* Governor Katie Hobbs proudly raised Pride flags at the State Capitol and has vetoed bills targeting LGBTQ+ Arizonans and signed executive orders protecting LGBTQ+ state employees and barring state agencies from supporting conversion therapy for minors.
* Attorney General Kris Mayes has made clear that her office will protect the civil rights of LGBTQ+ Arizonans, including taking action against discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity.
* Every Arizona Democrat in Congress in 2022 voted for the Respect for Marriage Act, protecting federal recognition of same-sex marriages.

That is the difference Democratic leadership makes. The Arizona Democratic Party is organizing year-round to elect leaders who will defend our freedoms, protect our communities, and build a state where everyone belongs, no matter who they are or who they love. This Pride Month, I am asking you to make a contribution to help us keep building that power. Your donation will help us register voters, support pro-equality candidates, train volunteers, reach communities across Arizona, and make sure Democrats have the resources they need to win. Pride has always been about more than one month. It is about showing up, standing together, and refusing to go backward. As someone who believes deeply in this work — and as someone whose own life has been shaped by the progress generations before us fought for — I am grateful to be in this fight with you. Please make a contribution today to support the Arizona Democratic Party this Pride Month. With pride, Joey Czajkowski

body:
[](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260610-1.c5b4Uh&refcode=em20260610-3399&t=1&akid=3399%2E21716%2ElIuGx2)
**I’m Josh Turek. I’m a Democratic state legislator who won a deep red seat, four-time Paralympian, and two-time gold medalist in wheelchair basketball.**
I thought the feeling of winning my first gold medal at the 2016 Rio Paralympics would only come once in a lifetime. But, then my race was called:
_**I’m officially the Democratic nominee for Iowa’s open U.S. Senate seat.** _
Grassroots energy usually peaks in the first few days after a primary, so we have to get down to business ASAP. [**Will you help me make the most of our hard-fought victory by splitting a donation between my campaign and Sarah McBride to become one of the first Founding Donors of my General Election campaign?**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260610-1.c5b4Uh&refcode=em20260610-3399&t=2&akid=3399%2E21716%2ElIuGx2)
**[Split a donation »](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260610-1.c5b4Uh&amount=5&refcode=em20260610-3399&t=3&akid=3399%2E21716%2ElIuGx2)**
I’m honored that the people of Iowa have put their faith in me, and I’m ready to take this once-in-a-generation shot to win this OPEN seat and be the champion working people deserve in Washington.
**I got into this race because like millions of fellow Democrats, I was fed up with losing, fed up with treating “red” states like lost causes and tired of perpetually playing defense.**
I won this primary because I played offense, and **I’m going to run a relentless full-court press to win this seat in November.**
I don’t take a penny of corporate PAC money. Your support, and your support _alone_ , will help us flip Iowa blue for the first time in more than a decade and take back the Senate Majority.
[**I’m personally asking you to become one of our first General Election Founding Donors by splitting a contribution of $15, $20, $35, or more today. Your contribution will power my voter outreach so I can flip Joni Ernst’s Senate seat and restore hope and faith in the great state of Iowa.**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260610-1.c5b4Uh&refcode=em20260610-3399&t=4&akid=3399%2E21716%2ElIuGx2)
**[Split a donation »](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260610-1.c5b4Uh&amount=5&refcode=em20260610-3399&t=5&akid=3399%2E21716%2ElIuGx2)**
Look, I’m under no illusions about the work it’ll take to win a battleground Senate race as a Democrat in Iowa. Taking on Joni Ernst, Ashley Hinson, and their billionaire-fueled MAGA Machine will be a beast of a challenge — physically, mentally, financially.
But I’m not your average career politician. I’ve won back-to-back victories in deep red Trump country. Polls show me either tied with or one point ahead of my official Republican opponent, Ashley Hinson.
**This election will be a nail-biter, and it starts right now.**
We have **5 months** to bring independents and conservatives into our Prairie Populist coalition; to overcome over $40 million in spending from MAGA megadonors; and to let the world know that working-class Americans own the future.
Ads, statewide tours, and campaign infrastructure don’t come cheap, and our campaign coffers are nearly empty after a hard-fought and high-cost primary victory.
The outcome of this race will decide the Senate majority with huge implications for our country, so my team and I need every single solitary ounce of support to hit the ground rolling. [**Will you rush a split contribution to become one of my first General Election Founding Donors in this high-stakes Senate race ASAP?** ](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260610-1.c5b4Uh&refcode=em20260610-3399&t=6&akid=3399%2E21716%2ElIuGx2)
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260610-1.c5b4Uh&amount=5&refcode=em20260610-3399&t=25&akid=3399%2E21716%2ElIuGx2)**
We have a ton of work to do and history to make here in Iowa.
Let’s do this.
Talk soon,
Josh Turek

The outcome of this race will decide the Senate majority with huge implications for our country, so my team and I need every single solitary ounce of support to hit the ground rolling. We have a ton of work to do and history to make here in Iowa. Let’s do this. Talk soon, Josh Turek

name: Melat Kiros
subject: $350,000 in dark money attack ads just entered the chat
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Justice Democrats
body:
Help me kick them out of Denver for good.
#
Last week, we got word that Diana DeGette was openly signaling for super PACs to enter this race and run attack ads against me.
Well, today we found out one of them answered.
**[A newly created super PAC has announced it’s spending $350,000 on ads to smear me with outright lies. What makes it even worse is that we have no idea who is paying for it.](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260610-mk.kSXmCu&refcode=em20260610-37890&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=2&akid=37890%2E1203867%2EItf66R)**
**[FIGHT BACK](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260610-mk.kSXmCu&refcode=em20260610-37890&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=3&akid=37890%2E1203867%2EItf66R)**
This super PAC didn't exist a month ago. There is virtually no public information about its donors, no way for voters to know whose interests are behind these attacks, and zero accountability for the people writing the checks.
And that's exactly how dark money is supposed to work.
It could be the pharmaceutical companies and insurance lobbyists who have spent years investing in Diana to protect their profits. Or it could be AIPAC, disguising their influence by funneling money through yet another shell PAC, as they’ve done multiple times over the last several years. It could be the weapons manufacturers like Lockheed Martin, who donated thousands to Diana earlier this year and are invested in our country continuing to pursue wars forever.
Maybe it's another special interest entirely! We genuinely don't know.
But what we do know is that Diana DeGette spent last week sending a very public message that she wanted outside groups to come into this race and attack my supporters and me. Now, just days later, a mystery super PAC has appeared with hundreds of thousands of dollars to do exactly that.
A politician who feels secure in her record doesn't need anonymous special interests to rescue her campaign, but that's what happens when a grassroots campaign like ours starts to become a serious threat to their power.
People are asking why Denver is represented by someone who has spent nearly thirty years in Congress while housing costs soar, health care remains unaffordable, and private equity rakes in record-breaking profits.
The people funding these ads may be able to hide their identities, but they can't hide what they're afraid of. They're afraid that Denver voters might decide they want something different.
We don't have corporate PACs or anonymous billionaires spending hundreds of thousands of dollars on our behalf. We’ve got people.
**[If we're going to fight back against $350,000 in dark money attacks, it's going to take thousands of ordinary people stepping up right now. Can you split a contribution between Justice Democrats and my campaign today to help us respond?](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260610-mk.kSXmCu&refcode=em20260610-37890&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=4&akid=37890%2E1203867%2EItf66R)**
**[Contribute $10](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260610-mk.kSXmCu&refcode=em20260610-37890&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=23&akid=37890%2E1203867%2EItf66R)**
Bring. It. On.
– Melat

**Dear Patriot,** Ever since its drafting, the Declaration of Independence has sparked debate. First it was a dispute about separation from the Crown; later it was an argument about equality and its meaning. Our American debate — using the Declaration as a touchstone for our principles — has driven abolition, women's suffrage, and the civil rights movement. This debate continues today as we get ready to celebrate our nation's 250th birthday.
## A Book for This Moment
I'm writing today because two of BRI's own — President and CEO **David J. Bobb** and Senior Fellow **Tony Williams** — have written something I think deserves a place in every library. _Divided Over the Declaration: How an Enduring Debate Sustains the Vision of America_ will be released **June 9**. Their book takes readers into the rooms, streets, battlefields, churches, and courtrooms where the Declaration's meaning was contested, defended, and renewed. Thomas Jefferson under impossible pressure. Abigail Adams demanding the nation not forget the women. Frederick Douglass in Rochester, 1852, insisting America be held to its own promise. This is the story of what it actually cost, and what it actually took, to move this country closer to its founding ideals. It's the kind of history BRI believes in: honest, rigorous, and ultimately hopeful about what America is capable of becoming.
## Support BRI. Receive the Book.
BRI's free resources, teacher training, the Civics Innovation Lab, and student programs don't happen without your support. July 4, 2026 is just weeks away. This is the school year, and the national moment, we have been preparing for. And the work doesn't stop when the bunting comes down on July 5. First it was a dispute about separation from the Crown; later it was an argument about equality and its meaning. Our American debate — using the Declaration as a touchstone for our principles — has driven abolition, women's suffrage, and the civil rights movement. This debate continues today as we get ready to celebrate our nation's 250th birthday. A Book for This Moment I'm writing today because two of BRI's own — President and CEO David J. Bobb and Senior Fellow Tony Williams — have written something I think deserves a place in every library. Divided Over the Declaration: How an Enduring Debate Sustains the Vision of America will be released June 9. Their book takes readers into the rooms, streets, battlefields, churches, and courtrooms where the Declaration's meaning was contested, defended, and renewed. Thomas Jefferson under impossible pressure. Abigail Adams demanding the nation not forget the women. Frederick Douglass in Rochester, 1852, insisting America be held to its own promise. This is the story of what it actually cost, and what it actually took, to move this country closer to its founding ideals.
